observation.visible_scene: A clear plastic bag filled with water and a single koi fish (white body with red-orange patches, lying horizontally with its head toward the right end) rests on a gray tiled tabletop. The bag's left end is gathered and tied off with an orange band, and the plastic shows condensation droplets with a yellowish water layer at the bottom. A long-haired brown-and-white cat with white chest, white paws and long white whiskers sits at the right edge of the table, initially with its muzzle pressed against the bag's pointed right tip where the fish's head is.
visible_changes: The cat lifts its head away from the bag's tip and reorients its face from downward-sniffing to upright, turning toward the camera and then glancing back down at the bag.
The cat shifts its seated body slightly, moving its paws and torso a little rightward/backward on the tile, ending in a still, upright sitting posture looking at the bag.

The camera reframes (pans/zooms out), so the tied left end of the bag slides out of view to the left and background items (a terracotta pot, white pebbles, table legs) appear at the top, while the bag and cat move leftward within the frame.
The koi fish remains in a largely fixed pose inside the bag throughout; any apparent displacement is dominated by the camera reframing rather than visible swimming.
The bag itself does not visibly deform or move on the table apart from the camera-induced shift in frame position.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the bag to be placed on the table, and whether the cat ever makes contact with or opens the bag after this excerpt.
The fish's behavior or condition outside this window, and the outcome of the cat's interest.
Whether the bag was moved or merely re-framed by the camera before/after the clip.
uncertain_details: The leftward drift of the bag and cat in frame is ambiguous between camera pan and physical translation; background tile seams and table-edge position support camera movement.
Fine motion of the fish (gill/fin movement) cannot be confirmed against the plastic and water distortion.
Whether the cat's head-lift is a deliberate disengagement or just a momentary posture change is not determinable from the frames alone.
